name: room
text: Room opened — goal: improve: Self-improvement: review prompts/engines/routing/own-code; auto-apply safe changes; pitch

name: Sprocket
text: Do it: Add a "safe patch" rule to auto-apply only formatting tweaks (spaces, line endings, trailing commas) to our own codebase. The trade-off is we accept zero logic changes, but gain consistent style without manual review. This keeps our focus on meaningful improvements while eliminating noise.

name: Gauge
text: The real risk isn’t just "skipping deeper logic fixes"—it’s that formatting-only patches auto-applied to our own code become a crutch, masking deeper inconsistencies we never surface. A better alternative is to auto-apply *only* formatting tweaks to *third-party* dependencies, where style drift is noise, not a signal of technical debt. Settle it by proving the third-party case first—then revisit our own codebase with stricter guardrails.
